meta.name: Is It Done Yet
meta.note: Values are read from the reference, not invented. Anything derived says so in `derived`. The Unity importer (unity/Assets/IsItDoneYet/Design/Editor/DesignTokenImporter.cs) reads this file and writes a DesignTokens ScriptableObject; it is the single source of truth for both.
meta.colorSpaceNote: Every hex here is sRGB, exactly as the CSS wrote it. The Unity project renders in Linear, so each one must go through sRGB->Linear on import. Assigning a hex straight to a Color in a Linear project produces a visibly washed-out result -- see design/DEVIATIONS.md.

ink.note: The single outline colour. Every panel, chip, pill and icon in the headset screens is stroked in this and nothing else.

ink-warm.note: The title and loading screens outline in this warmer brown instead. Two outline colours by context, deliberately.

background.note: Backdrop of the headset screens. In MR this is passthrough; the token exists for the Design Gallery.

background-paper.note: The title screen's paper ground, with a 135deg hairline stripe over it.

surface.note: The cream panel fill. The most-used colour in the design after the ink.

surface-sunken.note: A row recessed inside a panel: leaderboard entries, skipped ingredients.

surface-rail.note: The bottom control rail. Same value as the ink, which is what makes the rail read as a cut-out rather than a panel.

accent.note: Primary. Display headings, the primary CTA, the score.

accent-2.note: Secondary CTA and badges. The only fill that carries ink-coloured text at display size.

danger.note: Pink chip fill. Notice it is a PALE fill with dark text, never a saturated red block -- the design never shouts.

text-body.note: Paragraph text on a cream panel. Softer than `text-primary`, which is reserved for headings and labels.

text-on-accent.note: Supporting text on the red panel.

outline-soft.note: Dashed borders: optional items, secondary title-screen buttons.

divider.note: The 3px dashed rule inside a panel.

counter-wood.note: The rendered countertop. Scenery, not UI.

panel-sheen.note: Not a CSS gradient -- the reference fakes depth with inset box-shadows. Reproduced in the panel shader as a vertical ramp: a bright top lip and a darkening foot.

radius.note: Read off the reference: 14 on a list row, 18 on a stat tile, 26 on a panel, 34 on the hero card. `circle: -1` means half the smaller side.

border.note: The border scales WITH the element: a chip takes 3, a panel 5, the hero card 6. A uniform border width is the single fastest way to lose this design's look.

shadow.note: The signature. Two hard offset copies of the silhouette in near-black plus one real blur, and two insets for the lip and the foot. No soft drop shadow alone -- that reads as generic material design and loses the sticker feel entirely.

spacing.note: Even numbers throughout the reference. Padding on a panel is 20-22, on a chip 7x16, gap between cards 16-18.

display.name: Ranchers
display.note: All caps in every use. Never set lowercase -- the face is designed for it and reads wrong otherwise.

type.note: Tracking is in em, as CSS letter-spacing. The uppercase labels carry 0.14-0.18em and that wide tracking is a large part of the design's character.

overshoot.note: Taken verbatim from the loading screen's gravity stack. This is the curve that makes the design feel like it has weight; use it for anything that lands.

squash.note: The reference's landing animation squashes on impact and rebounds. Encoded so a Unity tween can reproduce it rather than approximate it.

safety.note: Nothing may flash above this. No large high-contrast full-field flashes at any rate.

xr.note: Meta's own guidance, encoded as hard floors. Sources in design/README.md. A dmm is 1mm at 1m, so a size in dmm is an angular size and stays legible at any placement distance.

contrast.note: Measured, not assumed. WCAG 2.1 relative luminance over the sRGB values above; recomputed by tools/design-extract/contrast.mjs. Recorded because the reference is a web design and a Quest panel is read at a distance through passthrough, where a pairing that was merely decorative on a monitor becomes unreadable.
contrast.rule: A pairing below 4.5:1 may only carry text at display sizes. The panel shader's text outline exists so that the floor holds against passthrough as well as against the panel fill.

SAFE.note: For steps flagged hot or knife. The HUD collapses to one calm pill and gets out of the way.
derivationRules: accent := accent-2 (#FBD24B). Gold on the ink is the highest-contrast pair in this palette, and red reads as an alarm on a step where the cook is already holding a knife.
text-on-accent := text-primary, since gold needs dark text.
typeScale := 1.25. Larger type is the point: this theme is read at a glance, from further away, while holding something.
motionScale := 0.35 and loopingAnimation := false. Nothing may move in the corner of the eye of somebody near heat.
panelOpacity := 1.0, because a translucent panel over a bright hob is unreadable.
danger stays as-is. Suppressing the one colour that means 'stop' to calm the palette would be the wrong kind of calm.

accent := #2F6DA8, derived by taking the palette's cool pair (fill #C4DAEE, ink #2F4D68) and finding the saturated midpoint that carries #FFF3E4 text. This colour is NOT in the reference -- it is the one value invented here, because practice mode must be unmistakable at a glance and no existing accent was free. Measured 4.95:1 against #FFF3E4, which beats the reference's own red-on-cream at 3.74:1.
accent-2 stays gold, so the secondary CTA does not move under the cook.
A PRACTICE badge is always on screen. A mode that changes what a score means must never be inferred from a hue alone -- somebody colourblind gets the word.
